LoloBuy rehearsal parcel: what should you verify before shipping?

Use pre-packing results to review parcel weight, dimensions and route fit before you submit the actual package.

⌕

Shipping and parcel preparation · 10 minute read

LoloBuy rehearsal parcel: use the preview before the real shipment

A LoloBuy rehearsal parcel is a pre-packing preview, not an international shipment. That distinction matters. The current interface describes rehearsal as a simulation service that creates no real parcel. It is designed to pre-pack selected warehouse items and estimate the packed weight, dimensions and freight basis before the buyer uses the separate Submit Package action.

The result can answer a useful question: what might this exact group of stored items look like after packing? It can reduce guesswork when several products, retail boxes or protective materials make the final parcel difficult to predict. It does not lock a delivery time, guarantee customs acceptance or turn an estimate into a carrier invoice.

This guide explains when the rehearsal step is worth considering, what information to prepare, how to read the result and which details still need checking before actual parcel submission.

1. Decide whether you need a rehearsal parcel

A rehearsal is most useful when the difference between loose item data and packed parcel data could affect your shipping decision. Examples include several warehouse items going into one package, bulky retail packaging, irregular shapes, fragile products that may need more protection, or a route with size and weight limits. A buyer comparing available routes may also want a better packed measurement before choosing one.

It is less useful when you have not finished checking the products. Complete ordinary QC review, any additional-photo request and any return or exchange decision first. Pre-packing an item that you may still reject creates an avoidable extra step. The rehearsal should answer a parcel question, not replace product inspection.

Write down the decision you expect the result to support. For example: “Can these three stored items fit a route’s published limits?” or “Does keeping the shoe boxes change the chargeable basis enough to reconsider packaging?” A clear question prevents you from treating the result as a general promise.

2. Verify the selected warehouse items

Start in My Warehouse and identify every item you intend to include. Match the warehouse item number, product title, selected specification and quantity to your order records. Check that each item is in a state that allows it to be selected. The rehearsal record has an item list, so use that list as an audit trail rather than relying on thumbnails alone.

Make a simple manifest with one row per warehouse item. Record the item number, SKU, quantity, existing weight and dimensions if shown, QC decision, and whether retail packaging must stay. If two items look similar, this list helps prevent selecting the wrong color or size. Save it before creating the rehearsal request.

Do not assume that every stored product can travel on every route. Batteries, liquids, magnets, branded goods, food and other restricted categories may be treated differently by a carrier or destination. The current freight estimator asks for a destination and product categories and then presents available lines and their limits. Route eligibility still needs to be checked for the actual goods.

3. Give packaging instructions that can be followed

The rehearsal record can include a packaging service and notes. Make those instructions concrete. State which retail boxes must be kept, which removable packaging may be discarded, which items need separation and where extra protection is important. Avoid a vague instruction such as “make it small but safe.” Compact packing and stronger protection can pull in opposite directions.

For fragile items, identify the vulnerable part: glass surface, corner, buckle, lens or electronic screen. For shoes or collectibles, say whether the retail box is part of the purchase value. For soft clothing, say whether presentation or reduced volume is the priority. Only request services that appear in the live account and suit the selected route; available options and their charges can change.

Keep a copy of the submitted note. If the result differs from your request, you can compare the packed outcome with the exact instruction instead of reconstructing it from memory.

4. Select an intended line without treating it as final

The current rehearsal workflow includes an intended shipping line. That gives the warehouse useful context because different routes may have different size, weight, category or packaging rules. Before selecting a line, enter the destination and review the current route details in the freight estimator.

Check the line’s product eligibility, minimum and maximum weight, dimension limits, billing standard and prohibited-item information. Do not choose by the displayed estimate alone. A cheaper-looking line that cannot accept the item category or packed dimensions is not a usable option.

Treat the rehearsal line as the line you want evaluated, not a permanent reservation or a delivery guarantee. Availability and eligibility must be checked again when the real parcel is submitted. If the completed rehearsal points to a different line, compare the live requirements rather than assuming the old choice will transfer automatically.

5. Understand actual, volumetric and chargeable weight

The rehearsal result may show estimated actual weight, parcel dimensions and volumetric weight. Actual weight is what the packed parcel weighs. Volumetric weight converts the space a parcel occupies into a weight figure under a route’s billing rule. Chargeable weight is the figure the route uses to calculate freight.

The official estimator can describe routes that charge by actual weight, by volumetric weight, or by the greater of the two. It can also display a route-specific volumetric formula. Do not copy a single divisor from an old article and apply it everywhere. Read the live billing standard for the selected line because the rule belongs to that route.

Suppose a parcel is light but large because it keeps several retail boxes. Its volumetric figure may exceed its scale weight on a route that compares both. Removing unnecessary packaging could change the dimensions more than the actual weight. A dense parcel may behave differently. The rehearsal result helps reveal which side of that comparison deserves attention.

6. Track the rehearsal status before acting

Creating the request is not the same as receiving a result. LoloBuy currently shows separate rehearsal states, including Pending Payment, Pending Processing, Outbound, Processing, Completed, Committed, Canceled and Expired. Read the description attached to the record instead of guessing what work has finished.

Pending Payment means the rehearsal has been submitted but payment is still pending. Pending Processing means payment has completed and the request is waiting for warehouse handling. The processing states indicate that the outbound slip or warehouse work is underway. Completed is the point at which the interface says the parcel can be submitted. Committed means an actual parcel has already been submitted from the rehearsal record.

Canceled and Expired are not completed results. The current expired description can appear when the item list contains an order that can no longer be submitted. If a status seems inconsistent with the item records, save the rehearsal number, item numbers and screenshots before contacting support. Do not invent a processing deadline; use the live status and account messages.

7. Read the completed rehearsal as an estimate

When the rehearsal is complete, compare its item list with your manifest. Confirm that the correct items and quantities were packed. Then record the rehearsal number, intended line, packaging service, estimated actual weight, dimensions and any displayed volumetric weight or billing statement.

Next, compare the result with the route limits. Check every dimension, not only the longest side. Recheck category eligibility and any packaging restriction. If the result says charges would be based on volumetric weight, identify whether removable outer packaging is driving the size. If it says actual weight, confirm that all requested protective material is represented before using the figure for budgeting.

LoloBuy’s current reminder says rehearsal weight and volume are estimates for reference. Packaging materials, item condition and value-added services can make outbound data fluctuate. Therefore, use the result to narrow your decision, not to promise an exact final freight amount.

8. Convert the preview into an actual package carefully

A completed rehearsal does not ship itself. Use the separate Submit Package action when you are ready to create the real parcel. Reconfirm the destination address, recipient details, selected delivery line, packaging choice, declared goods, quantities, declared values, tax information where applicable, and any available protection option.

The submission interface explains that initial payment can be based on estimated chargeable weight. After packing, the warehouse confirms actual weight or volume; if the final shipping fee differs, the account may receive a notice about a refund or additional payment. This is another reason not to present the rehearsal estimate as the final charge.

After submission, verify that the rehearsal record moves to Committed and links to the expected parcel. Keep the rehearsal number and parcel number together. They refer to different stages and make support questions easier to trace.

9. Investigate a mismatch with evidence

If the result contains the wrong item, unexpected dimensions or an unclear packaging outcome, pause before submitting. Compare the rehearsal item list with your warehouse manifest and saved note. Capture the full result screen, not just the number that looks wrong. Include the rehearsal number, affected item number, expected instruction and visible result in one concise support message.

Ask a narrow question: which packaging was used, whether a listed item was included, or which measurement belongs to the packed parcel. Avoid demanding a promised price or delivery date from rehearsal data. The service previews packing; it does not control later carrier scans, customs decisions or delivery events.

Final LoloBuy rehearsal parcel checklist

Before rehearsal, finish QC, confirm each warehouse item and write packaging priorities. Select an intended line only after checking the destination, item eligibility and current limits. When the result arrives, verify the item list, packaging service, actual weight, dimensions, volumetric weight and billing basis. Treat every figure as a pre-shipment estimate.

Before the actual parcel, check the live route again, review the address and declaration, understand how the final chargeable weight will be determined and save both record numbers. The most useful rehearsal is not the one with the smallest number. It is the one that exposes a packing or route issue while you can still change the shipment plan.
